note: How operators become agents. A user prompt first opens or reuses the host-bound v2.2 session with scripts/session-open.mjs, before scope confirmation. One invocation of one operator is one attempt in the mode its operator.json declares. The orchestrator freezes request.expected, request.frozenInputs and request.environment, calls scripts/attempt-gate.mjs open, acquires the one session-wide scheduler through scripts/worker-slots.mjs, then starts the agent. Acceptance calls scripts/attempt-gate.mjs accept, which reruns the frozen request, the shared response contract and the operator validator. A matched receipt may advance; mismatch is retained and chooses repair, retry or blocked. Nested exchanges and retries use the same host session, attempt ledger and three worker slots. A chain route adds prerequisite work to the same dynamic chain rather than opening another user session. The orchestrator's memory is state.json.brief and nothing else.

modes.inline: the orchestrator runs the operator's Steps itself, in the chat, in order, with the operator's own grants, and runs both validators on what it wrote; no agent is created; the profile recorded is the orchestrator's own
modes.dispatch: one new agent that inherits the orchestrator's transcript (the profile's forkTurns.dispatch turns), on the operator's profile, with the brief (operators/<id>/brief.md) and request.json as its instruction; at most concurrency.maxDispatch such agents at a time; awaited on its completion event, never on a timer
modes.isolated: one new agent with an empty context (forkTurns.isolated is none), on the operator's profile, that sees only brief.md, request.json and the files request.inputs and request.contexts name, in its own worktree and browser profile; awaited on its completion event, never on a timer

wait: completion: a dispatched or isolated agent is awaited on its completion event and a chain route on its sibling session's end; a timed poll is not a step of any chain, and a wait that returns nothing is not evidence of anything

budget.note: written into state.json.budget at create; a request past a cap is BUDGET_EXHAUSTED and the person answers a budget-choice (narrow, continue, stop) recorded in state.json.choices; continue is recorded as a budget.extensions entry; when a plan branch produced a units.json, the orchestrator counts its N journey units — the units a verifying lane will be dispatched over, scripts/validate-request.mjs#budgetUnitsOf — and raises maxSteps to maxSteps + perUnit × N at that transition, so a fan-out is paid for by the coverage it takes and a unit the plan deferred costs nothing, being an unchecked entry on the ledger rather than a branch (scripts/validate-session.mjs#unitBudgetErrors)

fixSize.note: the line between interface.fix and interface.generate, in count, in kind and in patience. Count: a fix moves at most maxFiles declared paths, creates and deletes none, and writes only classes the frozen inventory publishes (operators/interface-fix/validate.mjs#fixSizeErrors). Kind: a finding whose rule is published under a generateTopics folder of knowledge/ui, or whose rule prefix is in generatePrefixes, is a composition or a taste decision and goes to interface.generate however small its patch would be; every other rule (a presentation value, a proof measurement, a UAT step) is fix-eligible (scripts/validate-request.mjs#fixKindErrors). Patience: after escalateAfter interface.fix branches for one finding in a session, the next repair of that finding is interface.generate, never another fix

helpers.note: The support layer beside the operators. A helper never creates a user session. Its v2.2 helper-run binds hostBinding to the existing Codex task or Claude session and carries starciSessionId when a mission owns it. It writes no product source, touches no runtime, publishes nothing and asks nothing. When it runs concurrently it acquires from the same host session worker gate; waiting releases the slot. A helper that finds it must write product source, touch a runtime or publish has found an operator's job and stops.
helpers.writes: alias/alias.json is the one home of the support write set: a Writes alias of a helper is an alias the registry marks helperWritable, which no product source route, no runtime owner and no publication target carries (scripts/validate-helper.mjs)
helpers.toolsNote: the closed set of tool modes the support layer may hold, and the one home of it: reading is a helper's whole authority, so git stops at read and every mode that writes a checkout, operates a runtime, publishes to a registry or resolves a secret is absent rather than declared never
helpers.stepVerbsNote: a Steps row of a helper opens with one of these verbs, so its procedure reads as a procedure and not as a description of a state; the list grows when a helper needs a verb it lacks, never a second list
helpers.bank: What a helper drafts, the orchestrator takes from: @worktrees/banked/<product> (scripts/bank.mjs, alias/alias.json). The person approves one queue once — the choice bank:<product>:v<n> in approvals.json, over the queue hash — and that answer is the goal-confirm of every mission the queue lists: a session opened from a banked entry writes state.json.mission from the entry's goalDraft unchanged, records its own goal-confirm choice with the approval as sourceRef, prints the block and does not wait (SKILL.md step 1). The orchestrator is the only writer of queue.json during a run: it marks the entry running:<sessionId> when it opens the session and done:<sessionId> when the session ends done, and it takes only what scripts/bank.mjs#next hands back — the first banked entry whose every dependsOn is done, and nothing at all while a sibling of the same product is running, so one mission of a product runs at a time and a mission that stopped for the person pauses the bank by staying running. Nothing in a bank pins a head: each mission preflights and plans its own chain when it opens. A goal corrected at open time is not covered by the approval: the bank entry is rewritten, which changes the queue hash, which ends the approval, and the person is asked again (scripts/validate-session.mjs#bankRefErrors).

agent.grants: operator.json → resources.tools: each @tools/<id> with one mode from resources/tools.json, and nothing the profile would otherwise permit. A tool whose only use the operator's mode forbids is not granted for that run: backend.generate and interface.generate under mode dry receive neither @tools/sourcewrite nor @tools/git
agent.refs: operator.md → Context table, resolved through alias/alias.json; an unlisted location is unreadable
agent.requirements: operator.md → Requirements table; fill defaults into request.json and obtain required values from the mission, existing decisions and declared inputs. Fields under agent.fills (project, runId and lease) come from the session. A missing default does not itself authorize a question: apply interactionPolicy. Unavailable required authorization still blocks under the existing operator gate; this communication rule supplies no grant.
agent.prompt: rendered at dispatch (mode dispatch or isolated) from operators/<id>/brief.md (generated, at most briefBytes) plus request.json; the agent reads operator.md sections through @tools/fileread for the step it is on; never stored
agent.isolation: per resources.mode: isolated starts with no inherited turns and sees only what request.json names; dispatch inherits the orchestrator's transcript for forkTurns.dispatch turns of its profile; inline is the orchestrator itself
agent.writes: only response/ of its own branch (step-N/parallel-M/response/); a nested-exchange agent writes only <exchange>/response/ of that branch; a source-writing operator also writes the session branch of its checkout under an exclusive lease (see sourceWrites)
agent.profileRecord: the orchestrator fills response.json boundProfile (operator.json → resources.profile) and ranProfile at dispatch whenever the two differ; validate-response refuses one without the other or a boundProfile that is not the operator's

concurrency.rule: scripts/worker-slots.mjs is the executable session-wide gate: at most maxConcurrentAgents active workers across top-level branches, nested exchanges, helpers, repairs and retries. A wait releases its slot. A branch queues when its inputs are not accepted or its normalized exclusive resource overlaps a live lease, including parent/child paths and Windows case variants.
concurrency.gate: node scripts/worker-slots.mjs acquire|resume <branch> <workerId>; node scripts/worker-slots.mjs release <session> <token>
concurrency.state: state.json.workerSlots and state.json.leases, mutated with scripts/session-lock.mjs
concurrency.dispatchRule: at most maxDispatch agents in mode dispatch at once, because each one carries the orchestrator's transcript and two such transcripts diverge; isolated agents are bounded only by maxConcurrentAgents
concurrency.sharedCheckout: two agents may read one checkout; only one may hold it for writing (backend.generate, interface.generate, git.publish are exclusive per checkout)
concurrency.sharedRoot: business.decide is exclusive per businesses root; runtime.serve is exclusive per runtime owner, identity.provision per provider realm, data.seed per flow namespace

handoff.carrier: response.json fields: kind → path relative to the branch; the next branch's request.json inputs point at step-N/parallel-M/<path> from the session root, written explicitly by the orchestrator (nearest earlier producer guides the orchestrator, never the agent)
handoff.stop: response.json status blocked with stop = code; errors/ says whether the code terminates or falls back, and routing.json says where a terminated step hands to. A code the merged registry does not list is read by the orchestrator as UNKNOWN_STOP and routed on domain caller; the branch keeps the code the agent wrote as evidence and the orchestrator records the substitution in state.json.substitutions
handoff.waiting: response.json status waiting with awaiting { exchange, kind }: the orchestrator validates the fields written so far, creates <exchange>/request/request.json in the same branch, runs a new agent for it in the operator's own mode, and resumes the paused agent when <exchange>/response/response.json is done; other branches of the step keep running
handoff.resume: a blocked branch re-enters the same operator as a new agent in step-(N+1)/parallel-1, with request.json.resume naming the blocked step and parallel; the blocked branch stays on disk as evidence
handoff.chain: a stop whose routing.json route is kind chain adds the target owner and its prerequisites to a replanned version of this session's chain, preserving the confirmed goal and hostBinding. The blocked attempt waits without a worker slot and re-enters as a new attempt after the added branch produces a validator-accepted input. It never creates a second user session.
handoff.skeleton: at dispatch the orchestrator writes response/response.json with status running and the branch's identity fields; the agent's first act on finishing is replacing it; an exit that leaves it in place is followed up once, then recorded as blocked with RECEIPT_MISSING and event abandoned

session.manifest: Every new state.json carries contractVersion starci/v2.2, hostBinding { kind, hostId, worktree, sourcePromptRef }, lifecycle, a versioned mission with the eight-row scope data and explicit confirmation, attempts, workerSlots, leases, chain, steps, planned, requestHashes, choices, transitions, brief and budget. scripts/session-open.mjs writes the draft before confirmation and reuses it by hostId plus absolute worktree. Legacy unmarked state remains readable evidence but cannot dispatch through the v2.2 gates.
session.branch: step-<N>/parallel-<M>/ — N is the position in the chain, M the parallel branch; parallel-1 always exists
branchLayout: response/<other>.md when the operator has one
session.paths: inside request.json inputs: from the session root (step-1/parallel-1/response/response.md); inside response.json fields and operator.md Outputs: from the branch (response/response.md, critique/response/critique.md)

imports.note: imported producer slots (scripts/producer-import.mjs) live at step numbers from stepBase upward, a range no chain reaches: a chain is numbered from 1 and a slot below stepBase is refused at import, so a chain that grows past its planned length never collides with the evidence it was planned on; a chain cell that names an evidence slot's coordinate is refused by validate-chain

lifecycle: open: node scripts/session-open.mjs open <sessionsRoot> <draft.json> creates or reuses the host user session before asking. The draft mission stores Goal, Target, In scope, Out of scope, Outputs, Done when, Verification reach and Example. The same authorized user prompt may be recorded as the versioned as-stated answer; corrected or rejected never activates it.

branch: write request.json with contractVersion, attempt, expected, environment and frozenInputs; node scripts/attempt-gate.mjs open <branch> freezes it and writes the running skeleton; node scripts/worker-slots.mjs acquire <branch> <workerId> must return acquired before execution.

advance: node scripts/attempt-gate.mjs accept <branch> reruns validate-request, validate-response and the operator validator. status done advances only with a matched comparison for every required expected criterion and resolvable evidence. status mismatch preserves the receipt and chooses repair, retry or blocked; the next attempt points at it and cannot weaken required expected under the same goal version.

abandon: an agent exited with the running skeleton in place; one followup_task to the same agent naming the skeleton; a second exit writes status blocked with stop RECEIPT_MISSING, event abandoned, and the chain routes it as caller
wait: status waiting releases the worker slot. The nested exchange opens its own attempt under the same session and cap; worker-slots resume reacquires a slot before the parent continues.

block: status blocked keeps the session on disk. When routing.json answers the stop's domain with kind resume, the orchestrator asks the person for the field the stop names and re-enters the operator in step-(N+1)/parallel-1 with resume set and state.json.resumes recorded. When it answers operator, the named operator runs next and the blocked branch is re-entered the same way once that operator is done. When it answers user or external, the branch stays blocked and the chain continues only after the person or the outside party has changed something the stop names; that continuation is also a step-(N+1)/parallel-1 re-entry with resume set, and request.json must carry the changed requirement or input, because a re-entry with no delta is NO_PROGRESS

close-success: goal achieved, operator done and git.publish do not close the user session. Only an explicit successful session-close signal calls scripts/session-cleanup.mjs. It writes and verifies @worktrees/done/<id>.md and @worktrees/done/<id>/bundle first, then deletes exactly sessions/<id>. Blocked, failed, waiting and active sessions remain resumable; no user worktree or branch is removed.

report: every turn the orchestrator ends with a person is one of resources/interaction.json#reportShapes in the display language (resources/settings.json#language over settings.example.json, default vi; interaction.json#language), recorded in brief.report; a hand-off to a peer session is a waiting branch with a wake condition in brief.peers, never the end of a turn

sourceWrites.rule: an operator that writes source (interface.generate, interface.fix, backend.generate, library.update) writes only on the session branch session/<sessionId> of the routed checkout, in a git worktree the orchestrator prepared from the frozen head; it commits the declared write set once and records the sha in response.json.commits; the person's checked-out branch is never touched
sourceWrites.track: changes.md names every path with before/after hashes and the commit; the next requests pin @workspaces/<role> at that sha (contexts[].head) so quality.verify and interface.audit verify exactly what was written
sourceWrites.publish: git.publish merges the session branch into the target branch: fast-forward when the target has not moved; a merge commit only when there is no conflict and the gates are re-run on the merge result; a conflict is NON_FAST_FORWARD and a person resolves it; never rebase, never force
sourceWrites.cleanup: Publication never closes or cleans a user session. On an explicit close-success event, scripts/session-cleanup.mjs writes and verifies @worktrees/done/<sessionId>.md plus <sessionId>/bundle/{state.json, retained request/response/evidence/import files}, then removes only @worktrees/sessions/<sessionId>. It never removes a user worktree, branch, sessions root or central-runtime; blocked, failed and waiting sessions remain resumable.
sourceWrites.history: a source-writing operator runs the request preflight before it writes any file outside the session folder and records its verdict and instant in `## Binding` of changes.md as `Preflight` (`<passed|failed> at <ISO 8601 instant>`), beside `Reflog before` and `Reflog after` (`HEAD <reflog entries> <head sha>; stash <reflog entries>`) read at dispatch and at its last commit; a routed checkout gains only that branch's own commits, so a stash, a reset, a force, a clean, a checkout of another branch, a rebase or an am inside one is refused, a temporary worktree is removed with `git worktree remove --force`, and nothing under a checkout whose `node_modules` is a junction is deleted by hand
sourceWrites.policy: the routed checkout must declare gitPolicy.worktreeBranches = session-only (readiness/initialization/workspaces); a route declaring forbidden binds read-only and no source-writing operator may run against it; mode dry is exempt, because it writes nothing: a dry backend.generate or interface.generate may run against a read-only binding, and its plan records a null commit

profileEquivalents.rule: an operator binds one profile; when the processor runs on a runtime that lacks that profile, it runs the equivalent profile of its own runtime with exactly the grants the operator requires, and response.json records both (boundProfile, ranProfile) so an audit can tell a stand-in from the binding
profileEquivalents.grants: the equivalent runs with the tools the operator declares that its own profile permits and its runtime supports (resources/tools.json); a tool the runtime does not support is unavailable for that run: a judged imagegen step records that no artwork could be made and continues, any other unsupported tool blocks the branch with the operator's own code
profileEquivalents.imageVersusVisualize: imageGeneration means artwork: a digital image produced by an image model (OpenAI profiles only). Rendering HTML (direction candidates, audit sheets, previews) is visualization, needs no grant, and every runtime does it.
